reasons: The cited paragraphs (p0132, p0137) show only an investigation right tied to suspected breaches of Customer content/acceptable-use warranties, with an attempt-to-notify undertaking; they confer no audit, inspection or record/system access right over Customer usage.

With no audit right binding the Customer, our position is better than the preferred position, so 'compliant' is the correct classification and inserting an audit framework would create a right the Vendor does not have — no redline or comment is expected for a compliant finding, and none was proposed.
The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is an artifact of there being no audit clause to parametrize, not evidence of a deviation.
Rationale correctly notes the §11.3 investigation right as a residual observation rather than escalating it as a deviation, consistent with the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements.
